title: Penguin was 'uneasy' with criticism of govt in my memoir: Sonia Gandhi
description:
Breaking her silence on the censorship row involving her upcoming memoir, Congress Parliamentary Party chairperson Sonia Gandhi has said that publisher Penguin Random House India was "uneasy" with criticism of the government. While she was disappointed that the publisher did not go ahead with the book, she was not surprised.
Penguin Random House India (PRHI) was initially keen to publish the memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", but subsequently said it would not be the Indian publisher.
In an interview with The Guardian ahead of the release of the book on November 10, Gandhi said Penguin was "uneasy in general with the criticism of the government".
Gandhi admitted she was disappointed, though not altogether surprised, by Penguin India's decision not to publish the book.
She saw it as an attempt to censor her book, The Guardian reported.
